title: Allocator leak slow-burn: isolation & mitigation logbook
content:
Summary:

Night shift (2024-11-06 23:30 UTC) we observed a slow degradation of throughput in the west-1 dedicated GPU pool over ~6 hours. No single catastrophic failure — instead a steady increase in request P99 latency (from ~180ms to ~520ms) and a proportional drop in tokens/sec per pool. Autoscaler began oscillating as node free memory dipped and eviction churn increased.

Why this doc exists (quick):
- Capture oncall timeline and quick-isolation commands used.
- Draft a runbook entry for 'allocator leak / slow-burn memory pressure' in ephemeral slots.
- Track mitigations that worked and those that didn't.
- Decide followups and who owns next actions.

Initial signals and detection:
- Metrics: pool.p99_latency_upstream, pool.tokens_per_sec, allocator.free_bytes (per-host), evictions/sec
- Alert that fired: dedicated-pool-p99-up (threshold 400ms sustained for 5m) -> paged SRE.
- Secondary signal: sudden rise in allocator.fragmentation_ratio on subset of nodes (not cluster-wide).
- Heap sampling via runtime/allocator sampler showed a slowly increasing active allocation footprint for a small set of tenants.

Oncall actions taken (chronological):
1) 23:35 UTC: Paginated, started voice. Grabbed list of hosts with allocator.free_bytes < 2GB.
   - command: curl -s api.internal/pools/west-1/hosts | jq '.[] | select(.allocator_free_bytes < 2147483648)'
2) 23:40 UTC: Identified 7 hosts with anomalous per-host tenant allocation heatmaps; top contributor was tenant T-1972 (heavy rerank workload, long context windows).
3) 23:50 UTC: Isolated tenant to preemptible lane via routing override to reduce new requests to that tenant (temporary mitigation).
   - command: POST /routing/override {tenant: "T-1972", route: "preemptible"}
4) 00:10 UTC: Ran live eviction on the 3 most impacted hosts to free KV cache and see if throughput recovered. Immediate small improvement but flapping resumed after ~12m.
5) 00:30 UTC: Increased autoscaler hysteresis (scale-down delay) to 15m to prevent oscillation while investigating.
6) 01:00 UTC: Rolled a hotfix that added a sampling hook for allocator metadata to the /metrics endpoint (for faster triage next time).

What worked:
- Temporary routing override to preemptible lane reduced new allocation pressure and bought time.
- Increasing scale-down delay reduced oscillation and prevented repeated evictions.

What didn’t work / surprises:
- Standard host-level OOM metrics were not helpful; this was fragmentation/leak-like growth inside runtime allocator, not kernel OOMs.
- Evicting KV cache provided only temporary relief; underlying allocations were not reclaimed by simple eviction.

Hypothesis (post-shift):
- A tenant workload pattern (long-lived rerank calls with repeated cache pinning) is causing allocator growth due to a codepath that pins small GPU buffers for longer than intended (probable reference leak).
- This interacts poorly with our autoscaler because allocator_free_bytes is used indirectly by node capacity signals; fragmentation causes apparent short-term free memory even as usable contiguous blocks shrink -> triggers eviction -> eviction increases fragmentation -> positive feedback loop.

Immediate followups (owners):
- Miguel S. to reproduce locally with T-1972 traces and create a minimal repro: due 2024-11-12.
- Priya K. to add per-tenant allocator delta alerts (on ratio of allocated_bytes growth rate) and a dashboard tile: due 2024-11-14.
- Evan L. to propose an allocator metric that exposes 'largest_contiguous_block' per host so autoscaler can make better decisions: due 2024-11-18.

Runbook draft snippets (for SRE playbook):
- Detection: alert if pool.p99_latency > 350ms and host.allocator_fragmentation_ratio > 0.45 for >= 10m.
- Quick triage steps:
  1) identify hosts: api.internal/pools/{pool}/hosts | jq filter on allocator_free_bytes and fragmentation_ratio
  2) identify top tenants by allocation: runtime-tooling/top-tenant-allocs --host HOSTID --top 10
  3) temporarily shadow or route offending tenant to preemptible lane
  4) if immediate host-level recovery is needed: cordon host from scheduler for 5m and trigger eviction job (use with caution: evictions may amplify fragmentation)
  5) increase autoscaler scale-down delay to >= 15m in the pool
- Escalation: if > 30% of pool hosts show fragmentation_ratio > 0.5 escalate to infra-platform + applied-ml (possible model runtime bug).

Suggested permanent changes (proposal):
- Add 'largest_contiguous_block' to host metrics and feed it into autoscaler decisions.
- Add per-tenant allocation growth rate alert and a 'tenant soft-quota' that triggers routing throttles before evictions.
- Instrument allocator to emit sampled backtraces for long-lived allocations (to find leak sites).
- Add a canary that runs a simulated long-context rerank workload to detect regressions in allocator behavior during deploys.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Is this purely tenant-side (workload pattern) or also triggered by recent runtime PRs? (check PRs merged in prior 48h)
- Should we change autoscaler input to use fragmentation-aware capacity instead of raw free bytes?
- What SLA changes need customer communication for tenants hit by routing overrides?

Links & artifacts:
- Incident ticket: JIRA- RDW-2137
- Postmortem draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/allocator-leak-postmortem (work in progress)
- Runtime PR for metrics (hotfix): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/987

Notes to self (informal):
- capture heap samples next time earlier in the incident (we had sampling turned off for cost reasons)
- consider a short-lived debug build in prod that captures per-alloc stack traces when a host's fragmentation_ratio crosses 0.4
- remind product: long-context rerank customers may need guidance on concurrency vs context size tradeoffs

Appendix: quick commands used during triage:
- list bad hosts: curl -s api.internal/pools/west-1/hosts | jq '.[] | select(.allocator_free_bytes < 2147483648) | {host: .id, frag: .allocator_fragmentation_ratio, free: .allocator_free_bytes}'
- top tenants by alloc on host: runtime-tooling/top-tenant-allocs --host HOSTID --top 20 | head -n 40
- routing override: POST https://api.internal/routing/override -d '{"tenant":"T-1972","route":"preemptible","reason":"triage-2024-11-07"}'

End of logbook entry.

Next update: followups due by assigned owners; schedule a short-run followup sync (30m) once repro and metrics dashboard are available.
